entries.notes: CHECK-1's reading of the definition and the bridge stands. The paragraph at l.237 is unchanged up to '... conversely if every alpha^i > 0.' Appended: 'Unless a measure is named, an ergodic policy is one ergodic for a finite invariant measure equivalent to lambda, as in Theorems 3.4 and B.1.' (1) Consistency with the definition. The convention uses the defined notion, 'ergodic for mu', with mu a finite invariant lambda-hat ~ lambda whose existence it requires. It defines only the unqualified phrase, so the definition stands as it is. By isKernelErgodic_congr the convention is equivalent to: 'admits a finite invariant measure equivalent to lambda and is ergodic for lambda'. 'Unless a measure is named' keeps the bridge sentence ('ergodic for lambda', named) under the plain definition. So the paragraph draws the distinction the theorems need. An EGF policy with positive weights is ergodic for lambda, but it is an ergodic policy only with a finite invariant lambda-hat ~ lambda. (2) Consistency with Definition 3.1. The convention concerns policies. Definition 3.1's 'the group ... is ergodic for lambda' concerns a group and names its measure. Every use of 'ergodic' for the group or its action names lambda or says 'acts ergodically' (l.145, 233, 321, 342, 877, 888, 898, 908). No sentence calls an EGF's policy 'an ergodic policy' on the strength of Definition 3.1 alone. The name 'Ergodic Generative Flows' refers to Definition 3.1, not to the convention. There is no conflict. (3) 'As in Theorems 3.4 and B.1' is exact. Theorem 3.4 (l.305) has 'some pi* ergodic for a finite invariant measure equivalent to lambda'. B.1 (l.856) has 'admits a finite invariant measure lambda-hat equivalent to lambda for which it is ergodic'. This is the hypothesis of EGF.universal_iff_ergodic: lambda finite, pi Markov, lamHat finite with lamHat.bind pi = lamHat, lamHat << lam and lam << lamHat, giving IsUniversalPolicy lam pi iff IsKernelErgodic pi lamHat. The rendered references read 'Theorems 3.4 and B.1'. (4) l.240, 'There are two key ideas that motivate Definition~\ref{def:egf}:', removes the ambiguity (CHECK-1 finding 2). It renders as 'Definition 3.1'. The marker l.241 sits before the existing blank line, so the paragraphing is unchanged. (5) Register. added_hypotheses is unchanged: positive weights for the converse, present in the text. The convention is a naming convention, not a hypothesis of a statement. The two added anchors are the ones CHECK-1 finding 6b asked for.

convention_check.l286: 'The next theorem states that if the family contains an ergodic policy pi*, then the family is universal.' Under the convention: if the family contains a policy ergodic for a finite invariant measure equivalent to lambda, it is universal. That is Theorem 3.4's hypothesis on the policy (EGF.universality_of_ergodic_family, from EGF.universal_iff_ergodic). The dense outflows of Theorem 3.4 are left to the theorem, as in v1's paraphrase. The sentence is now true in the theorems' sense. The Sink counterexample of CHECK-1 (pi constant delta_true on Bool: ergodic for lambda, no invariant lambda-hat ~ lambda, EGF.Sink.not_isSummablyL2Mixing) is no longer an 'ergodic policy'.
convention_check.l298: 'Ergodicity alone ensures the convergence of phi pi^n only in the much weaker Cesaro sense, and this is enough for universality.' The subject is the kernel pi of Definition 3.3, and 'ergodicity' with no measure is the property the convention names. With a finite invariant lambda-hat ~ lambda: the Cesaro averages of P h = d((h lambda-hat)pi)/d lambda-hat tend to 0 on mean-zero L^2(lambda-hat) (EGF.Markov.tendsto_birkhoffAverage_densityActionL2). Since (phi lambda)pi^n = (P^n h) lambda-hat for h = phi d lambda / d lambda-hat, this is the Cesaro convergence of phi pi^n, in total variation in the form B.1's proof uses (EGF.exists_tvMass_cesaro_lt_of_ergodic). 'Enough for universality' is EGF.universal_iff_ergodic. The sentence is now true. Strictly, the convention defines the adjective 'an ergodic policy', and the noun 'ergodicity' of a policy is its natural extension. That is not worth a finding.
convention_check.l858: 'universality itself needs only ergodicity' sits inside B.1, where lambda-hat is named. Under either reading (ergodic for that lambda-hat, or the convention, equivalent by isKernelErgodic_congr) it is EGF.universal_iff_ergodic: ergodicity is sufficient and necessary. It is true.
convention_check.other_uses: No other unqualified use becomes false under the convention. l.260 (Expressivity, 'Ergodicity guarantees, for a model rich enough (Theorem 3.4), ...'): if 'Ergodicity' is a policy's, the convention makes it Theorem 3.4's hypothesis, which improves on CHECK-1's 'true through its pointer'. If it is the group's (Definition 3.1), it remains true through the pointer, as before. l.763's parenthesis ('one randomly initialized non-trainable translation is sufficient to ensure ergodicity') concerns generators, so the group: true by EGF.ae_ergodic_torusAffine_one and EGF.isGroupErgodic_of_ergodic_mem. Read for the one-move policy with alpha = 1, it is also an ergodic policy in the convention's sense: Haar measure is invariant and finite, and EGF.isKernelErgodic_deterministic applies. The abstract (l.123) and the Conclusion (l.783), 'leverage ergodicity', are informal. Every other use names its measure or concerns a group action.
